verses.1:1: Now it happened in the days when the judges judged that there was a famine in the land, and a man went from Bethlehem of Judah to reside as a foreigner in the fields of Moab—he, his wife, and his two sons.
verses.1:2: The man's name was Elimelech, his wife's name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion—Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah. They came to the fields of Moab and stayed there.
verses.1:3: Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left—she and her two sons.
verses.1:4: They took Moabite wives for themselves; the name of one was Orpah, and the name of the second was Ruth. They lived there for about ten years.
verses.1:5: Then both of them also died, Mahlon and Chilion, and the woman was left without her two children and without her husband.
verses.1:6: Then she rose, she and her daughters-in-law, and turned back from the fields of Moab, because she had heard in the countryside of Moab that the LORD had attended to His people by giving them bread.
verses.1:7: So she went out from the place where she had been, and her two daughters-in-law were with her, and they walked on the road to return to the land of Judah.
verses.1:8: Then Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, "Go, return, each woman to her mother's house. May the LORD deal in loyal love with you, just as you have dealt with the dead and with me.
verses.1:9: May the LORD grant you that you find a place of rest, each woman in the house of her husband." Then she kissed them, and they raised their voices and wept.
verses.1:10: And they said to her, "No, with you we will return to your people."
verses.1:11: But Naomi said, "Return, my daughters. Why should you go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb who could become husbands for you?
verses.1:12: Return, my daughters, go, for I am too old to belong to a husband. Even if I said, 'I have hope'—even if I belonged to a husband tonight and even bore sons—
verses.1:13: would you wait expectantly for them until they grew up? Would you hold yourselves back for them from belonging to a husband? No, my daughters, for it is far more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the LORD has gone out against me."
verses.1:14: Then they raised their voices and wept again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.
verses.1:15: She said, "Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods. Return after your sister-in-law."
verses.1:16: But Ruth replied, "Do not press me to abandon you, to turn back from following you. For to wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you spend the night, I will spend the night. Your people are my people, and your God is my God.
verses.1:17: Wherever you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD do thus to me, and thus add to it, if anything other than death separates me from you."
verses.1:18: When she saw that she was firmly resolved to go with her, she stopped speaking to her.
verses.1:19: So the two of them walked on until they reached Bethlehem. And it happened when they arrived in Bethlehem that the entire city was stirred up over them, and the women asked, "Is this Naomi?"
verses.1:20: She replied to them, "Do not call me Naomi; call me Mara, because the Almighty has made it exceedingly bitter for me.
verses.1:21: I left full, yet the LORD has brought me back empty-handed. Why do you call me Naomi, while the LORD has testified against me and the Almighty has brought harm upon me?"
verses.1:22: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, with her—the one who returned from the fields of Moab. And they arrived in Bethlehem at the start of the barley harvest.
verses.2:1: Now Naomi had a relative of her husband, a prominent man of worth from the clan of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.
verses.2:2: Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Please let me go to the field and glean among the heads of grain behind one in whose eyes I find favor." And she said to her, "Go, my daughter."
verses.2:3: So she went and arrived and gleaned in the field behind the reapers; and by chance she happened upon the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.
verses.2:4: Now look, Boaz arrived from Bethlehem, and he said to the reapers, "The LORD be with you." They replied to him, "May the LORD bless you."
verses.2:5: Then Boaz said to his young man who was set over the reapers, "To whom does this young woman belong?"
verses.2:6: The young man set over the reapers answered and said, "She is a Moabite young woman, the one who returned with Naomi from the fields of Moab.
verses.2:7: She said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.' So she came and has remained standing from the morning until now; this sitting of hers in the shelter has been only brief."
verses.2:8: Then Boaz said to Ruth, "Have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and do not leave from here either, but stay closely here with my young women.
verses.2:9: Keep your eyes on the field that they are reaping, and walk behind them. Have I not commanded the young men not to touch you? And whenever you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from what the young men draw."
verses.2:10: Then she fell on her face and bowed down to the ground, and she said to him, "Why have I found favor in your eyes, that you should take notice of me, when I am a foreigner?"
verses.2:11: Boaz answered and said to her, "It has been fully reported to me everything that you have done for your mother-in-law after the death of your husband, and how you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth and came to a people whom you had not known previously.
verses.2:12: May the LORD repay your deed, and may your reward be complete from the LORD, the God of Israel, beneath whose wings you have come to take refuge."
verses.2:13: She said, "May I find favor in your eyes, my lord, because you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your servant girl, even though I am not like one of your servant girls."
verses.2:14: At mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come over here, eat from the bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar." So she sat beside the reapers, and he passed her roasted grain; she ate, was satisfied, and had some left over.
verses.2:15: When she rose to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not humiliate her.
verses.2:16: Furthermore, be sure to pull out some for her from the bundles and leave it so that she may glean it, and do not rebuke her."
verses.2:17: So she gleaned in the field until evening. Then she beat out what she had gleaned, and it came to about an ephah of barley.
verses.2:18: She lifted it up and went into the city, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. She also brought out and gave to her what she had left over after being satisfied.
verses.2:19: Her mother-in-law asked her, "Where did you glean today, and where did you work? May the one who took notice of you be blessed." So she told her mother-in-law with whom she had worked, and she said, "The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boaz."
verses.2:20: Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "May he be blessed by the LORD, who has not forsaken His loyal love toward the living and toward the dead." Then Naomi said to her, "The man is a close relative of ours; he is one of our redeemers."
verses.2:21: Then Ruth the Moabite said, "Furthermore, he even told me, 'Stay closely with my young men until they have finished all of my harvest.'"
verses.2:22: Naomi said to Ruth, her daughter-in-law, "It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that no one accosts you in another field."
verses.2:23: So she stayed closely with Boaz's young women to glean until the completion of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest, and she lived with her mother-in-law.
verses.3:1: Then Naomi, her mother-in-law, said to her, "My daughter, should I not seek a place of rest for you, that it may go well for you?
verses.3:2: Now, is not Boaz our relative, whose young women you have been with? Look, he is winnowing barley at the threshing floor tonight.
verses.3:3: Therefore wash yourself, anoint yourself, put on your garments, and go down to the threshing floor. Do not let yourself be known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
verses.3:4: And when he lies down, note the place where he lies; then go in, uncover his feet, and lie down. He himself will tell you what you should do."
verses.3:5: She answered her, "Everything that you say to me, I will do."
verses.3:6: So she went down to the threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.
verses.3:7: When Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was glad, he went to lie down at the edge of the grain heap. Then she came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
verses.3:8: And it happened in the middle of the night that the man was startled and turned over, and look, a woman was lying at his feet.
verses.3:9: He asked, "Who are you?" She replied, "I am Ruth, your maidservant. Spread your wing over your maidservant, for you are a redeemer."
verses.3:10: Then he said, "May you be blessed by the LORD, my daughter. You have made your later loyal love even better than the first, by not going after the young men, whether poor or rich.
verses.3:11: And now, my daughter, do not fear. Everything that you say I will do for you, for the entire gate of my people knows that you are a woman of worth.
verses.3:12: Now, it is indeed true that I am a redeemer, yet there is also a redeemer who is closer than I.
verses.3:13: Stay the night, and in the morning, if he will redeem you, good—let him redeem you. But if he does not desire to redeem you, then I myself will redeem you, as the LORD lives! Lie down until the morning."
verses.3:14: So she lay at his feet until the morning, yet she rose before one person could recognize another. And he said, "Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."
verses.3:15: Then he said, "Bring the shawl that is on you and hold it." So she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and placed it upon her; then he went into the city.
verses.3:16: When she came to her mother-in-law, she asked, "Who are you, my daughter?" Then she told her everything that the man had done for her.
verses.3:17: And she said, "He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said to me, 'Do not go empty-handed to your mother-in-law.'"
verses.3:18: Then she said, "Sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter falls out, for the man will not be at rest unless he finishes the matter today."
verses.4:1: Meanwhile, Boaz went up to the gate and sat there, and look, the redeemer about whom Boaz had spoken was passing by. He said, "Turn aside, sit down here, so-and-so." So he turned aside and sat down.
verses.4:2: Then he took ten men from among the elders of the city and said, "Sit here." And they sat down.
verses.4:3: Then he said to the redeemer, "Naomi, who returned from the territory of Moab, is selling the parcel of the field that belonged to our brother Elimelech.
verses.4:4: And I thought I would disclose this to you, saying, 'Acquire it before those sitting here and before the elders of my people.' If you will redeem it, redeem it; and if it will not be redeemed, tell me so that I may know, for there is no one apart from you to redeem it, and I am after you." He said, "I myself will redeem it."
verses.4:5: Then Boaz said, "On the day you acquire the field from the hand of Naomi, you also acquire it from Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the dead man, to raise up the name of the dead man upon his inheritance."
verses.4:6: Then the redeemer said, "I cannot redeem it for myself, or I might ruin my inheritance. You redeem my right of redemption for yourself, for I cannot redeem it."
verses.4:7: Now this was done formerly in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to ratify any matter: a man would pull off his sandal and give it to his neighbor; and this was the attestation in Israel.
verses.4:8: So the redeemer said to Boaz, "Acquire it for yourself." And he pulled off his sandal.
verses.4:9: Then Boaz said to the elders and to all the people, "You are witnesses today that I have acquired everything that belonged to Elimelech, and everything that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi.
verses.4:10: And I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, for myself as a wife, to raise up the name of the dead man upon his inheritance, so that the name of the dead man will not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses today."
verses.4:11: And all the people in the gate and the elders said, "We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman entering your house like Rachel and like Leah, the two of whom built the house of Israel. Prosper in Ephrathah and make a name in Bethlehem,
verses.4:12: and may your house become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, from the seed the LORD will give you from this young woman."
verses.4:13: Then Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He went in to her, and the LORD granted her conception, and she gave birth to a son.
verses.4:14: And the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the LORD, who has not deprived you of a redeemer today; and may his name be proclaimed in Israel.
verses.4:15: He will be a restorer of life to you and will sustain your old age, for your daughter-in-law, who loves you, has borne him—she who is better to you than seven sons."
verses.4:16: And Naomi took the child, placed him in her lap, and became his caregiver.
verses.4:17: And the neighboring women gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi!" And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
verses.4:18: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez became the father of Hezron.
verses.4:19: And Hezron became the father of Ram, and Ram became the father of Amminadab.
verses.4:20: And Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon became the father of Salmah.
verses.4:21: And Salmon became the father of Boaz, and Boaz became the father of Obed.
verses.4:22: And Obed became the father of Jesse, and Jesse became the father of David.

notes.1:8: The ketiv writes the full imperfect form ya'aseh, while the qere reads the shortened jussive form ya'as ("May the LORD deal").
notes.1:13: The Niphal verb te'agenah ("hold yourselves back") occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible; the phrase mar-li me'od mikkem can mean either "far more bitter for me than for you" (comparative min) or "exceedingly bitter for me on your account" (causal min).
notes.1:17: The oath clause literally reads "if death separates between me and you," an elliptical Hebrew oath idiom standardly understood as "if anything other than death" (though some render "if even death").
notes.1:20: Naomi plays on the meanings of the names: Naomi (from a root meaning "pleasant") versus Mara ("bitter"), echoed by the Hiphil verb hemar ("has made it bitter").
notes.2:1: The ketiv reads meyuda' or mida' (an acquaintance), while the qere reads moda' ("a relative"); the phrase "man of worth" uses chayil, the same term Boaz later applies to Ruth ("woman of worth," 3:11).
notes.2:7: The final clause of the Hebrew text literally reads "this is her sitting in the house a little," a concise expression understood as referring to a brief rest in the field shelter.
notes.2:10: Ruth creates a wordplay between the Hiphil infinitive lehakkireni ("take notice of me") and nokhriyyah ("foreigner"), both derived from the Hebrew root nkr.
notes.2:20: The pronoun "His" follows the nearest grammatical antecedent, the LORD (compare Gen 24:27), though the Hebrew clause could also refer to Boaz; "redeemer" translates Hebrew go'el, a close kinsman responsible for protecting a family's property and line.
notes.3:3: Two ketiv/qere variants occur here: ketiv singular "your garment" versus qere plural "your garments" (simlotayikh), and ketiv weyaradti (preserving an archaic second-person feminine ending -ti) versus qere weyaradt ("and go down"); the same archaic ending appears in 3:4 (ketiv weshakhavti, qere weshakhavt, "and lie down").
notes.3:5: The words "to me" (elay) are qere wela ketiv, read in the Masoretic vocalization tradition though absent from the consonantal text (the same occurs in 3:17).
notes.3:9: Hebrew kanaf ("wing") also denotes the corner or edge of a garment; Ruth's request echoes Boaz's blessing in 2:12 ("beneath whose wings") while invoking a symbolic gesture of protective marriage.
notes.3:12: The particle im ("if") is ketiv wela qere, written in the consonantal text but omitted in the Masoretic reading tradition.
notes.3:15: Hebrew literally reads "six of barley," leaving the unit of measurement unstated, and the final verb wayyavo ("and he went") is masculine singular in the Masoretic Text, referring to Boaz.
notes.3:17: The words "to me" (elay) are Qere without Ketiv, read in the Masoretic vocalization tradition though absent from the written consonants (as in 3:5).
notes.4:1: Hebrew peloni almoni is an idiom for an unnamed person ("such-and-such a one"), deliberately withholding the redeemer's actual name.
notes.4:3: Hebrew makrah (Qal perfect of mkr, literally "has sold") denotes a resolved or imminent transaction, hence "is selling" (compare v. 5, where the field is still acquired from Naomi's hand).
notes.4:4: "Disclose this to you" renders the Hebrew idiom "uncover your ear." The MT reads 3ms Qal yig'al (rendered impersonally, "if it will not be redeemed") after 2ms tig'al, and the Qere reads cohortative we'ed'ah ("so that I may know") against Ketiv w'd'.
notes.4:5: Follows the Masoretic Qere (qanita, "you acquire") and cantillation (atnah on Naomi, keeping "Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the dead man" as a single appositional phrase governed by u-me'et, "and from"); the Ketiv reads qaniti ("I acquire"), and acquiring from Ruth entails taking her in levirate marriage (cf. 4:10).
notes.4:20: The MT spells this name Salmah here (compare "Salma" in 1 Chr 2:11) and Salmon in 4:21.

native_verses.3:14: So she lay at his feet until the morning, yet she rose before one person could recognize another. And he said, "Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."
native_verses.3:15: Then he said, "Bring the shawl that is on you and hold it." So she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and placed it upon her; then he went into the city.
native_verses.3:16: When she came to her mother-in-law, she asked, "Who are you, my daughter?" Then she told her everything that the man had done for her.
native_verses.3:17: And she said, "He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said to me, 'Do not go empty-handed to your mother-in-law.'"
native_verses.3:18: Then she said, "Sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter falls out, for the man will not be at rest unless he finishes the matter today."
native_verses.4:1: Meanwhile, Boaz went up to the gate and sat there, and look, the redeemer about whom Boaz had spoken was passing by. He said, "Turn aside, sit down here, so-and-so." So he turned aside and sat down.
native_verses.4:2: Then he took ten men from among the elders of the city and said, "Sit here." And they sat down.
native_verses.4:3: Then he said to the redeemer, "Naomi, who returned from the territory of Moab, is selling the parcel of the field that belonged to our brother Elimelech.
native_verses.4:4: And I thought I would disclose this to you, saying, 'Acquire it before those sitting here and before the elders of my people.' If you will redeem it, redeem it; and if it will not be redeemed, tell me so that I may know, for there is no one apart from you to redeem it, and I am after you." He said, "I myself will redeem it."
native_verses.4:5: Then Boaz said, "On the day you acquire the field from the hand of Naomi, you also acquire it from Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the dead man, to raise up the name of the dead man upon his inheritance."
native_verses.4:6: Then the redeemer said, "I cannot redeem it for myself, or I might ruin my inheritance. You redeem my right of redemption for yourself, for I cannot redeem it."
native_verses.4:7: Now this was done formerly in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to ratify any matter: a man would pull off his sandal and give it to his neighbor; and this was the attestation in Israel.
native_verses.4:8: So the redeemer said to Boaz, "Acquire it for yourself." And he pulled off his sandal.
native_verses.4:9: Then Boaz said to the elders and to all the people, "You are witnesses today that I have acquired everything that belonged to Elimelech, and everything that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi.
native_verses.4:10: And I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, for myself as a wife, to raise up the name of the dead man upon his inheritance, so that the name of the dead man will not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses today."
native_verses.4:11: And all the people in the gate and the elders said, "We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman entering your house like Rachel and like Leah, the two of whom built the house of Israel. Prosper in Ephrathah and make a name in Bethlehem,
native_verses.4:12: and may your house become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, from the seed the LORD will give you from this young woman."
native_verses.4:13: Then Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He went in to her, and the LORD granted her conception, and she gave birth to a son.
native_verses.4:14: And the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the LORD, who has not deprived you of a redeemer today; and may his name be proclaimed in Israel.
native_verses.4:15: He will be a restorer of life to you and will sustain your old age, for your daughter-in-law, who loves you, has borne him—she who is better to you than seven sons."
native_verses.4:16: And Naomi took the child, placed him in her lap, and became his caregiver.
native_verses.4:17: And the neighboring women gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi!" And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
native_verses.4:18: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez became the father of Hezron.
native_verses.4:19: And Hezron became the father of Ram, and Ram became the father of Amminadab.
native_verses.4:20: And Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon became the father of Salmah.
native_verses.4:21: And Salmon became the father of Boaz, and Boaz became the father of Obed.
native_verses.4:22: And Obed became the father of Jesse, and Jesse became the father of David.

native_notes.1:8: The ketiv writes the full imperfect form ya'aseh, while the qere reads the shortened jussive form ya'as ("May the LORD deal").
native_notes.1:13: The Niphal verb te'agenah ("hold yourselves back") occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible; the phrase mar-li me'od mikkem can mean either "far more bitter for me than for you" (comparative min) or "exceedingly bitter for me on your account" (causal min).
native_notes.1:17: The oath clause literally reads "if death separates between me and you," an elliptical Hebrew oath idiom standardly understood as "if anything other than death" (though some render "if even death").
native_notes.1:20: Naomi plays on the meanings of the names: Naomi (from a root meaning "pleasant") versus Mara ("bitter"), echoed by the Hiphil verb hemar ("has made it bitter").
native_notes.2:1: The ketiv reads meyuda' or mida' (an acquaintance), while the qere reads moda' ("a relative"); the phrase "man of worth" uses chayil, the same term Boaz later applies to Ruth ("woman of worth," 3:11).
native_notes.2:7: The final clause of the Hebrew text literally reads "this is her sitting in the house a little," a concise expression understood as referring to a brief rest in the field shelter.
native_notes.2:10: Ruth creates a wordplay between the Hiphil infinitive lehakkireni ("take notice of me") and nokhriyyah ("foreigner"), both derived from the Hebrew root nkr.
native_notes.2:20: The pronoun "His" follows the nearest grammatical antecedent, the LORD (compare Gen 24:27), though the Hebrew clause could also refer to Boaz; "redeemer" translates Hebrew go'el, a close kinsman responsible for protecting a family's property and line.
native_notes.3:3: Two ketiv/qere variants occur here: ketiv singular "your garment" versus qere plural "your garments" (simlotayikh), and ketiv weyaradti (preserving an archaic second-person feminine ending -ti) versus qere weyaradt ("and go down"); the same archaic ending appears in 3:4 (ketiv weshakhavti, qere weshakhavt, "and lie down").
native_notes.3:5: The words "to me" (elay) are qere wela ketiv, read in the Masoretic vocalization tradition though absent from the consonantal text (the same occurs in 3:17).
native_notes.3:9: Hebrew kanaf ("wing") also denotes the corner or edge of a garment; Ruth's request echoes Boaz's blessing in 2:12 ("beneath whose wings") while invoking a symbolic gesture of protective marriage.
native_notes.3:12: The particle im ("if") is ketiv wela qere, written in the consonantal text but omitted in the Masoretic reading tradition.
native_notes.3:15: Hebrew literally reads "six of barley," leaving the unit of measurement unstated, and the final verb wayyavo ("and he went") is masculine singular in the Masoretic Text, referring to Boaz.
native_notes.3:17: The words "to me" (elay) are Qere without Ketiv, read in the Masoretic vocalization tradition though absent from the written consonants (as in 3:5).
native_notes.4:1: Hebrew peloni almoni is an idiom for an unnamed person ("such-and-such a one"), deliberately withholding the redeemer's actual name.
native_notes.4:3: Hebrew makrah (Qal perfect of mkr, literally "has sold") denotes a resolved or imminent transaction, hence "is selling" (compare v. 5, where the field is still acquired from Naomi's hand).
native_notes.4:4: "Disclose this to you" renders the Hebrew idiom "uncover your ear." The MT reads 3ms Qal yig'al (rendered impersonally, "if it will not be redeemed") after 2ms tig'al, and the Qere reads cohortative we'ed'ah ("so that I may know") against Ketiv w'd'.
native_notes.4:5: Follows the Masoretic Qere (qanita, "you acquire") and cantillation (atnah on Naomi, keeping "Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the dead man" as a single appositional phrase governed by u-me'et, "and from"); the Ketiv reads qaniti ("I acquire"), and acquiring from Ruth entails taking her in levirate marriage (cf. 4:10).
native_notes.4:20: The MT spells this name Salmah here (compare "Salma" in 1 Chr 2:11) and Salmon in 4:21.
